scope: HL5 removes the 0.01% dead band only in jointly admitted affine Bayer components. No demosaic, profile, WB, format or language rewrite. Legacy retained; D40 and postponed point 6 excluded.
changes: Small positive lifts require agreement with every original nonsaturated measurement in an 18x18 neighbourhood, reduced at the active boundary: relative tolerance 0.001, floor 0.01, at least 12 measurements. No fitted coefficients or source ratios are changed.

All cells of an eight-connected clipped component must have admitted affine models and pass the additional check where a small lift is proposed; otherwise retain HL4 throughout the component. This prevents newly corrected islands.
Only exactly clipped sites can increase; valid RAW sites, negative/extended values, finite/four-times bounds and original-support requirements remain unchanged. X-Trans retains HL4 bit for bit.
The high bit of the admission map carries the decision. The bounded visit map and index queue fit the existing scratch peak and are released before mutation; memory reservations remain unchanged.
HL5 has a distinct shared recipe/cache key. Frozen HL4 recovery and guarded shared interpolation/edge sources keep the previous comparator reproducible.

global_dead_band_removal.metrics: Local RGB/gradient maxima; no common-chroma regression beyond 1e-5.
global_dead_band_removal.causal_limit: Better reconstructed samples can still increase demosaic peaks near a shoulder; not accepted on average scores.

rejected_variants.bayer_only_edit_execution_error: An initial exact-text edit failed to match formatted source. The intended restriction was not applied; X-Trans hash assertions caught it. Those two campaigns measured the global variant and were not treated as Bayer-only evidence.

cell_local_admission.metric: Gradient maximum from 0 to 0.000014424324 on two phases of a previously used signal.

fresh_verification.limits: 264 nonconstant new parameter realizations plus 88 ambiguity controls. Every RAW hash differs from development; 30 constant truth hashes recur in 32 control records. Phases, overlapping regions and clean/noisy pairs are correlated. Compatibility matrices generate and interpret the signal: no measured camera accuracy.

tracked_HL2_peaks.scope: Follow-up of previously flagged comparisons only, not a fresh exhaustive HL2 campaign.

legacy_comparison.limits: Same RAW, references, geometry and WB per comparison; no exposure fitting. Counts are overlapping region/metric comparisons, not independent scene wins. Legacy retains advantages on rejected coloured boundaries, texture and fully clipped fields. Normalized chromaticity is unbounded for signed RGB near a small sum, not Delta E or calibrated truth. One decode per engine is functional evidence only.

timing.scope: Same process, same input bytes, same native geometry and gains; two source versions with identical opt-level=3/LTO=thin, alternating order. Input read and input/output hashing excluded; allocation, parse, unpack, HL, demosaic and matrix included. Warm OS caches; no IPC or GUI, no thermal control. One-repeat entries check full-output equivalence only.
timing.limits: Same executable, bytes, geometry, WB, opt-level=3/thin LTO. Three warmups and alternating order: D750 30 repetitions, D800 14-bit and RAF 10; other five inputs one pair for hashes only. No concurrent test/build/GUI campaign; ordinary OS background and thermal state uncontrolled, no cold-start test. Differences below 1% do not establish a speed improvement.

open: Ten tracked local peak comparisons on seven signals remain worse than HL2: X-Trans interpolation/noise and noisy Bayer colour.
The general dead-band removal remains unqualified on X-Trans and nonaffine Bayer components; preserving measured sites and colour has priority over mean scores.
Legacy still wins some coloured boundaries, texture and fully clipped fields. Uninformative clipped codes cannot uniquely identify missing hue or detail.
Physical profiles/targets, measured sensor plateaus, broader independent photographic colour evaluation, adequate X-T5 registration and memory-pressure/global gates remain open.
